title: A low transaction, stagnant price housing market will continue next year
gist: Oxford Economics expects the UK housing market to stay stagnant in 2027, with low transactions and flat nominal prices as mortgage affordability remains stretched, with prices about 11% overvalued on its new affordability index.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics' new buyer affordability index shows UK house prices roughly 11% overvalued based on mortgage payment affordability, up from 4% before the US-Iran conflict began, driven by a sharp rise in mortgage interest rates.
insights.speaker: Anusha Suthenthiran
insights.so_what: Mortgage-rate shock is the decisive factor behind the fall in approvals.

insights.claim: Other affordability metrics have been stable, and mortgage affordability has been the decisive factor pushing down mortgage approvals.
insights.speaker: Anusha Suthenthiran
insights.so_what: Watch swap rates, which transmit directly to mortgage pricing.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics thinks the Bank of England will ultimately tighten by less than market pricing implies, yet swap rates will take time to fall back and subdued wage growth will keep mortgage affordability stretched, keeping transactions low in 2027.
insights.speaker: Anusha Suthenthiran
insights.so_what: UK rate path is priced more hawkishly than the house view; relevant for gilts and housebuilders.

insights.claim: There is no evidence higher rates are raising financial stress among existing borrowers, and the lack of forced sales, less trading up and low housebuilding will reinforce low transactions while low supply keeps prices broadly flat in cash terms over the coming year.
insights.speaker: Anusha Suthenthiran
insights.so_what: Stagnation rather than crash: low volumes, flat prices.
